title: Cross-service telemetry enrichment and signature ADR
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This ADR specifies a cross-service contract for contextual telemetry enrichment and cryptographic signing of telemetry batches emitted by edge proxies, API gateways, runtimes, and background workers. The goal is to improve traceability, enable reliable downstream attribution in metric and event pipelines, and prevent accidental or malicious injection of telemetry that could skew SLO calculations or billing.

Context and problem

Redwood operates multiple tiers that emit telemetry: edge-proxy, ingestion gateways, runtime-coordinator, model runtime nodes, and background jobs. Current problems:

- Missing cross-service context: many metrics lack tenant, request-id, or model-version alignment.
- Unauthenticated telemetry: ingest pipeline must currently rely on IP allow-lists and downstream heuristics to reject malformed events.
- Attribution drift: cost, latency and error SLOs are misattributed when enrichment is inconsistent.
- Hard to audit: no standardized way to prove a telemetry batch originated from an authorized service instance.

Decision (what we are adopting)

We adopt a two-part contract:

1) Telemetry enrichment envelope: every emitted metric/event/trace span must include a minimal canonical enrichment set (tenant_id, request_id, service, instance_id, model_variant, model_commit, sequence_length_category, sample_rate_tag).

2) Batch signature header: batches submitted to telemetry-ingest must carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature header (X-RDW-Telemetry-Sig) computed over a deterministic canonical JSON of the envelope and the payload, using short-lived signing keys distributed by the Telemetry Key Service (TKS).

Rationale

- Deterministic enrichment enables reliable joins across metrics, traces and prompt telemetry.
- Cryptographic signing prevents easy injection and provides a verifiable audit trail for billing/forensics.
- Short-lived keys limit blast radius of key leakage and simplify rotation.

Contract details (required fields and formats)

1) Canonical enrichment object (required fields):

| field | type | description | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| tenant_id | string | Organization ID or account id | org-12345 |
| request_id | string | Global request id propagated from ingress | 7e4a2f1c-9b6d |
| service | string | Logical service name emitting the telemetry | edge-proxy |
| instance_id | string | Unique instance id (host/container) | host-10-2-1-7 |
| model_variant | string | Model variant name if inference-related | gptx-7b-q4 |
| model_commit | string | (optional) model artifact commit hash | f2c4a1b |
| sequence_length_category | string | short|medium|long bucket for request length | short |
| sample_rate_tag | string | sampler metadata, e.g. p=0.01 | p=0.001 |

Notes: implementations MAY include additional fields but MUST NOT remove or rename required fields. All field values must be UTF-8 strings.

2) Signature header

- Header name: X-RDW-Telemetry-Sig
- Value format: v1,hmac_sha256,<key-id>,<hex-signature>
- Signed input: canonicalized UTF-8 bytes of the object {"envelope":<enrichment>,"payload":<batch>} serialized with keys sorted lexicographically and without whitespace.
- Algorithm: HMAC-SHA256.
- Key lifecycle: keys are issued with TTL=4h by TKS. Producers fetch and cache keys. Consumers validate signatures and reject older-than-8h keys (to permit small clock skew).

Security & key management

- Telemetry Key Service (TKS) issues keys bound to service principal and environment. TKS enforces: allowed_services, max_ttl, rotation policies.
- All signing operations must be performed in a process isolated from public request paths to reduce accidental leakage.
- Audit logs: TKS must produce an audit event for each key issuance and revocation.

Alternatives considered

1) Mutual TLS between producers and ingest: rejected due to operational complexity for short-lived runtime containers and for private deployments (on-prem customers).
2) Public-key signatures (Ed25519): considered but rejected because HMAC allows key derivation and simpler server-side rotation with less CPU cost; we may add asymmetric signatures in a future iteration for long-term archival.

Consequences and risks

- Positive: improved attribution accuracy, stronger guardrails against forged telemetry, clearer audit trail for billing/regression analysis.
- Operational cost: implementing TKS, producer libraries and consumer validators will require ~3 engineer-months across eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime.
- Risk: mis-implemented canonicalization can cause false rejections; teams must adopt shared library to canonicalize consistently.

Implementation plan (high level)

1) Libraries and shameless adoption
   1. eng-platform builds a lightweight telemetry-enrichment library (go/python/java) that:
      - attaches canonical enrichment, computes signature, rotates keys.
      - exposes a local validation CLI and test harness.
   2. eng-serving-runtime and edge-proxy integrate library into runtime request path for emitted telemetry.

2) Telemetry Key Service (TKS)
   - Implement TKS as an internal service in the platform cluster. API: /v1/keys/issue, /v1/keys/rotate, /v1/keys/revoke. Keys stored in KMS-backed secure store.

3) Ingest-side validation
   - telemetry-ingest will perform signature validation as a pre-filter. Invalid/no-signature batches are relegated to a quarantine topic for manual review and are not counted in SLO aggregations or billing.

4) Rollout phases
   - Phase 0 (2 weeks): library baked and unit tests; TKS prototype; no enforcement.
   - Phase 1 (4 weeks): opt-in validation for selected non-critical services (console diagnostics, model-stats). Monitor rejection rate < 0.1%.
   - Phase 2 (6 weeks): enforcement for production services (edge-proxy, runtime-coordinator). Rejection policy: quarantine + 5% sampling allowlist for backfill.
   - Phase 3 (ongoing): expand to all telemetry producers and require signatures for billing-relevant metrics.

Validation & acceptance criteria

- Producer library used by 90% of high-volume producers within 8 weeks of release.
- Telemetry-ingest signature validation latency added <= 5ms median, <= 25ms p99.
- Ingest rejection rate due to canonicalization bugs <= 0.05% in Phase 1.
- Attribution error (measured as percent of cost tokens misattributed across tenants for a weekly snapshot) reduces by >= 70% after full rollout.

Operational runbook highlights

1) Quarantine workflow:
   - telemetry-ingest writes invalid batches to topic telemetry-quarantine. An on-call rotation in eng-platform will triage.
2) Emergency bypass:
   - TKS exposes a scoped emergency token issuance endpoint to allow temporary bypass for critical deployments; all emergency issuances must be followed by postmortem and key revocation.
3) Backwards compatibility
   - For 12 weeks after enforcement, telemetry-ingest will accept unsigned events from a configured legacy-producer allowlist and mark them with tag legacy=true to prevent accidental double-counting.

Ownership and maintenance

- Primary owner: eng-platform (Telemetry Guild)
- Secondary stakeholders: eng-serving-runtime, eng-infra, eng-observability
- Documentation owner: eng-platform (responsible for SDKs, examples, and validation CLI)

Metrics and dashboards to add

- telemetry.signature.accept_rate (per-service, tenant)
- telemetry.signature.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- telemetry.quarantine.count (daily)
- telemetry.enrichment.missing_fields.rate (per-field)

Appendix A: Canonicalization examples

Example signed header:
X-RDW-Telemetry-Sig: v1,hmac_sha256,key-20260305-1,9f8a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a

Example canonical JSON to sign (spaces removed, keys sorted):
{"envelope":{"instance_id":"host-10-2-1-7","model_commit":"f2c4a1b","model_variant":"gptx-7b-q4","request_id":"7e4a2f1c-9b6d","sample_rate_tag":"p=0.001","sequence_length_category":"short","service":"edge-proxy","tenant_id":"org-12345"},"payload":[{"metric":"inference.latency_ms","points":[[1677624000,18]],"tags":{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"us-west-2"}}]}

Appendix B: Example validation CLI (pseudo)

# validate_batch --input batch.json --sig "$X_RDW_TELEMETRY_SIG"
# exit code 0 == valid, 1 == invalid

Appendix C: Migration checklist

1) Publish libraries and TKS staging with docs and examples (eng-platform).
2) Run two-week integration pilot with model-stats and console diagnostics.
3) Add dashboards; monitor quarantine topic.
4) Communicate to all teams with timelines and support office hours.
5) Enforce for production telemetry and deprecate legacy allowlist after 12 weeks.

Related decisions

- This ADR complements: telemetry-ingestion-and-retention-guidelines-2025 and adr-telemetry-aggregation-retention-hierarchy-2026 (see Related Pages).

Questions for future work

- Evaluate asymmetric signatures for long-term archival and cross-organization sharing.
- Add cryptographic proofs linking telemetry to billing invoices.
